title: Heat Registry Freiburg: combined Hyperthermia and Radiotherapy in Oncology
summary:
Hyperthermia (heating tissue to 39-43 °C) can improve the effect of conventional radiation therapy and/or systemic therapies on tumor cells. When combined with radiation therapy, heat treatment can significantly reduce the radiation dose while still achieving a good therapeutic effect. This also makes it possible to repeat treatment after previous radiation.
The HEAT registry aims at improving the therapy in the long term by collecting and analyzing data on the treatment, its effects, and side effects for all patients treated with the combination of hyperthermia and radiation therapy, possibly in combination with systemic therapies. This includes data on the course of the disease and treatment, as well as on tolerability, side effects, and the effectiveness of the combination treatment. Ultimately, this serves to improve therapy and should help in making individual treatment decisions.
conditions: all patients treated with hyperthermia plus radiotherapy, regardless of the indication

interventions.name: Medical information from all patients treated with a combination of hyperthermia and radiation therapy in Freiburg, and in some cases also with parallel systemic therapies, is systematically recorded in the HEAT registry.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- hyperthermia treatment combined with radiotherapy
- signed informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
inability to consent
